A report for information regarding the

content:
That approval be given to:
 
1. 
To approve expenditure
of £4,266.50 (excluding VAT) for the emergency felling of
sycamore trees (Acer pseudoplatanus) confirmed as infected with
sooty bark disease (Cryptostroma
corticale) at Goodson's Holt, London
Road, Sleaford, and at Potterhanworth Road woodland,
Heighington.
 
2. 
To note the four trees already felled this financial
year at Mareham Lane, Sleaford, and
Westgate Copse at a cost of
£2,450.00, undertaken on health and safety grounds where
trees presented an immediate hazard.

The minutes of the meeting held on Tuesday
28th July 2026 were received for accuracy purposes.
 
Vote:
 
9 Votes For  0 Vote Against  1 Abstention
 
RESOLVED:
 
That the minutes of the Planning Committee
held on Tuesday 28th July 2026 were approved as a
correct record.

Application No. and Type:


25/1617/OUT Outline Application




Proposal:


Outline application for the erection of 2 no.
custom self build 2-storey dwellings with double garages with means
of access and layout to be considered.




Location:


Land off Lincoln Road and Spring Lane,
Leasingham, Sleaford




Applicant:


Mr and Mrs Peter French




Agent:


DBL Architectural Design




Reason
for Committee Consideration:


Request by Ward Member Councillor Andrew
Hagues on the basis of concerns over the impact of development on
the ability to maintain the ditch and drainage lagoon to the south
and the potential for the development to increase flood risk to
third parties including associated with the maintenance liabilities
for the on-site surface water drainage scheme.
Furthermore, to consider the suitability of
Spring Lane to accommodate two additional properties, specifically
concerns over restricted visibility, the lack of passing places and
footpaths and the associated risks to users of Spring Lane from
increased traffic movements.




 
The Principal Planning Officer presented the
application using maps, plans and photographs to demonstrate the
location and character of the site, as well as the material issues
identified in the agenda report. He also drew Members’
attention to the relevant national and local planning policies.
 
The application was deferred for procedural
matters from the Planning Committee meeting on Tuesday
28th July 2026, in order to facilitate a minor change to
the wording of the description of the development and to clarify
that matters of access and layout were for consideration and not
reserved. There were no other amendments/revisions to the
application and following the Planning Committee meeting in July
2026, local reconsultation of the amended description had been
undertaken and the description updated on the planning online
system.
 
Following the publication of the agenda for
this meeting, an addendum had been published which contained
details of a correction to the application description, as the
previous description of the development had been carried across to
this agenda pack. 
 
The proposal sought outline planning
permission for the erection of two custom self-build two storey
dwellings with double garages, as well as the means of access and
layout. Landscaping, appearance and scale matters were reserved.
The site was adjacent to the site granted planning permission for
nine dwellings under 20/0577/FUL.
 
The key issues of this application were:
· 
Principle of development.
· 
Highways.
· 
Drainage and flood risk.
· 
Visual amenity/impact upon heritage assets.
· 
Residential amenity/relationship to other land users.
· 
Ecology and biodiversity net gain.
· 
Energy efficiency and climate change.
· 
Trees and landscaping.
· 
Self-build and custom-build housing.
· 
Affordable housing provision.
 
The application was being considered by the
Committee as requested by Local Ward Member, Councillor A Hagues.
Leasingham Parish Council had raised objections to the application,
and five letters of objection had also been received, all of which
were detailed within the agenda. There were no objections raised by
the other statutory consultees and their comments were also
contained within the agenda.
 
The Principal Planning Officer advised Members
that the recent revisions to the National Planning Policy Framework
(NPPF) did not have any impact on the Officer report or the
application recommendation.  The Officer
assessment was contained within the agenda with the recommendation
for Authority to deal and approve the application subject to the
signing of a unilateral undertaking (to secure the plots as custom
self-build in relation to the exemption from Biodiversity Net Gain)
along with the necessary planning conditions.
 
The meeting then adjourned to allow the
registered speaker to address the meeting. Councillor A Hagues
spoke as Local Ward Member/Strong Community Advocate, and he raised
the following points:
· 
Disappointment that the previous application for nine dwellings had
been approved.
· 
Concerns about the width and safe access along Spring Lane, as it
was only 2.5 metres wide.
· 
The Committee would benefit from a site visit to Spring Lane to see
the issues and concerns raised.
· 
Concerns about the impact of the application on existing drainage
and flooding matters.
 
Councillor Hagues then answered a question
from the Committee. As there were no other registered public
speakers, the meeting then resumed formal session.
 
Members debated the application in detail,
considering the Officer’s report, presentation and statements
from the Local Ward Member/Strong Community Advocate. During the
debate, several Members of the Committee raised concerns about the
proposal including:
· 
The impact of the application on existing drainage and flooding
matters and whether the proposed mitigation measures, planning
conditions and the drainage plan would be sufficient and
successfully implemented. 
· 
The width of Spring Lane and safety for pedestrians using the Lane
for access, particularly children, as the primary school was
accessed via Spring Lane. Also, safety for vehicle movements as the
Lane was extremely narrow, with a bend in the road and could
require vehicles to reverse to allow other road users to pass
by.
· 
The proposed access to the site from Spring Lane.
· 
That the proposal might not satisfy Policy S48 in terms of the
ability to travel by foot or cycle.
· 
The lack of potential for works to improve and widen Spring
Lane.
· 
The management and enforcement of the proposed banksman via the
Construction Management Plan. 
· 
The option of an independent highway expert in providing an
assessment of the application, specifically the suitability of the
access from a safety perspective. 
· 
Agreement with the Local Ward Member/Strong Community Advocate
about the points of concern he had raised.
 
In response to questions from the Committee,
the Principal Planning Officer advised that:
· 
Spring Lane was a highway adopted and maintained by Lincolnshire
County Council that was already in use and provided access to a
number of differing points.
· 
To seek refusal of the application, there would need to be clear
evidence of severe highway impacts from the two proposed dwellings
only and not from any existing developments and land uses, which
already use Spring Lane – or in the case of the adjacent
scheme for nine dwellings would use Spring Lane upon completion of
the development.
· 
The proposed development was outside flood zones 2 and 3 and the
Drainage Strategy included onsite attenuation crates.
· 
There was scope for the Committee to strengthen pre-commencement
conditions.
· 
It was the Officer view, and the agenda report contained details of
how the application was compliant with Policy S48.
· 
There was no scope for further widening of Spring Lane as part of
the proposal before Members. This was not physically possible
within the bounds of the highway land. There had previously been
some widening works, and a passing place would be delivered as part
of the delivery of the separately approved nine
dwellings. 
· 
Lincolnshire County Council had not requested any improvement works
to Spring Lane as part of this application and the proposed
planning conditions were deemed as acceptable.
· 
The timings of the banksman could be revised if deemed necessary
and the current timings proposed in the draft Construction
Management Plan included avoiding nursery drop off and pick-up
times.
 
The Chairman explained that if the delivery
timings were too specific, at this stage, they could become
restrictive and cause issues when Reserved Matters were applied
for, so they needed to be somewhat flexible. He also reminded
Members that the development for nine dwellings had already been
approved, there was access to other services from Spring Lane and
that Lincolnshire County Council – Highways had considered
these matters. 
 
The Development Manager further clarified
that:
· 
In terms of Policy S48, the application site was well placed for
access by foot or cycling, that there were no objections raised by
Lincolnshire County Council and that other services were currently
being accessed by pedestrians.
· 
The Committee were able to request onsite or offsite highway
improvement works; however, in order to meet the legal tests for
planning conditions it would need to be demonstrated that the works
were necessary to overcome a reason for refusal of the application.
No such reason was raised by the Highway Authority.
· 
There was not scope to request the installation of a footpath or
other works due to the width of Spring Lane and Lincolnshire County
Council - Highways had not stated that this was necessary to make
the development acceptable in planning terms.
· 
Officers were satisfied that bespoke condition 5, which contained
details and timings for the banksman was sufficient and the
Council’s Enforcement Team would be responsible for
investigating should any issues arise.
· 
A third-party highways review of the application was possible but
the objective would need to be clear and reasonable particularly in
light of the Lincolnshire County Council – Highways position
of no objection. 
· 
An extension of time for the Council to determine the application
had previously been agreed by the Applicant and it would be
unreasonable to delay the decision further to obtain third party
highway consultancy advice, as this could be challenged by the
Applicant with potential cost implications for the Council in the
event of a non-determination appeal. 
 
The Council’s Legal representative
advised that Members would need to evidence any reasons for going
against the consultee response from Lincolnshire County Council -
Highways and that the Committee were not in possession of such
evidence. Lincolnshire County Council – Highways had assessed
the proposal, they were the technical experts and the Committee
objective would need to be clear.
 
During the discussion of this application,
whilst other Members of the Committee acknowledged and appreciated
the concerns raised by the Local Ward Member/Strong Community
Advocate and those raised by Committee Members during the debate,
it was also acknowledged that:
· 
A severe adverse impact on the transport network would be needed to
engage NPPF (2026) Policy TR6.
· 
Statutory consultee, Lincolnshire County Council as the lead
Highways Authority had not raised any objections to the
proposal. 
· 
There was no physical scope or requirement for highway
improvements.
· 
Nine other dwellings had previously been approved with access via
Spring Lane.
· 
Other services were currently being accessed by pedestrians,
cyclists and vehicles from and on Spring Lane.
· 
Refusal of planning permission would need to be justified to the
Planning Inspector at a Planning Appeal.
· 
There was no justifiable evidence, planning reasons or planning
policies to warrant refusal of the application contrary to Officer
recommendation.
 
It was therefore proposed and seconded that
planning permission be granted in line with the Officer
recommendation that Authority to Deal and approve be given to
Officers, subject to the signing of a unilateral undertaking to
secure the plots as custom self-build in relation to the exemption
from Biodiversity Net Gain.
 
Vote:
 
For: 5  Against: 2  Abstentions: 3
 
RESOLVED:
 
That Authority to Deal and approve be given to
Officers, subject to the signing of a unilateral undertaking to
secure the plots as custom self-build in relation to the exemption
from Biodiversity Net Gain.
 
And subject to the
following Conditions:
 
1. 
Application for approval of reserved matters shall be made to the
district planning authority not later than the expiration of three
(3) years beginning with the date of this permission and the
development shall be begun not later than the expiration of two
years from the final approval of the reserved matters or, in the
case of approval on different dates, the final approval of the last
matter to be approved.
 
Reason: To comply with the
provisions of Section 92 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990
as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase
Act 2004.
 
2. 
Details of the appearance, landscaping and scale, (hereinafter
called "the reserved matters") shall be submitted to and approved
in writing by the Local Planning Authority before any development
begins and the development shall be carried out as approved.
 
Reason: This is an outline
application only and such details must be approved before
development commences.
 
3. 
Any application for the approval of reserved matters shall adhere
to the access and layout details approved as part of this
application and shown on the approved plans listed. Specifically,
they shall show for the location of the dwellings and associated
access within Flood Zone 1 with no operational development in Flood
Zones 2 or 3a.
 
Reason: To ensure new
development is located within the sequentially preferable location
in respect of flood risk, to accord with Policy S21 of the Central
Lincolnshire Local Plan (Adopted 2023) and Policy F5 of the NPPF
(2026).
 
4. 
The permitted development shall be undertaken in accordance with a
surface water drainage scheme which shall first have been approved
in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall:
· 
be based on sustainable drainage principles and an assessment of
the hydrological and hydrogeological context of the
development.
· 
provide details of how run-off will be safely conveyed and
attenuated during storms up to and including the 1 in 100 year
critical storm event, with an allowance for climate change, from
all hard surfaced areas within the development into the existing
local drainage infrastructure and watercourse system without
exceeding the run-off rate for the undeveloped site;
· 
provide attenuation details and discharge rates;
· 
provide details of the timetable for and any phasing of
implementation for the drainage scheme; and
· 
provide details of how the scheme shall be maintained and managed
over the lifetime of the development, including any arrangements
for adoption by any public body or Statutory Undertaker and any
other arrangements required to secure the operation of the drainage
system throughout its lifetime.
 
No dwelling shall be
occupied until the approved scheme has been completed or provided
on the site in accordance with the approved phasing. The approved
scheme shall be retained and maintained in full, in accordance with
the approved details.
 
Reason: To ensure that the
permitted development is adequately drained without creating or
increasing flood risk to land or property adjacent to, or
downstream of, the permitted development to accord with policy S21
of the Central Lincolnshire Local Plan (Adopted 2023) and Policy F8
of the NPPF (2026).
 
5. 
The development hereby approved shall not be commenced until a
Construction Traffic Management Plan and Method Statement based on
the principles set out in the Construction Traffic Management Plan
submitted alongside the application, has been submitted to and
approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority which shall
indicate measures to mitigate against traffic generation and
drainage of the site during the construction stage of the proposed
development.
 
The Construction Traffic
Management Plan and Method Statement shall include;
· 
phasing of the development to include access construction;
· 
the maximum size of all delivery vehicles;
· 
timing of deliveries to take account of the adjacent primary school
and nursery;
· 
use of a Banksman to supervise all deliveries to and from the site
for the length of Spring Lane;
· 
the parking of vehicles of site operatives and visitors;
· 
loading and unloading of plant and materials;
· 
storage of plant and materials used in constructing the
development;
· 
measures to be implemented to prevent debris being deposited on the
public highway;
· 
the routes of construction traffic to and from the site (there
shall be no access directly from the A15).
 
The Construction
Traffic Management Plan and Method Statement shall be strictly
adhered to throughout the construction period.
 
Reason: In the
interests of the safety and convenience of users of the public
highway and residential amenity to accord with Policies S47 and S53
of the Central Lincolnshire Local Plan (Adopted 2023).
 
6. 
The development hereby approved shall not be commenced until an
Ecological Mitigation & Enhancement Plan (EMEP) in accordance
with the Preliminary Ecological Appraisal dated December 2025 by HS
Ecology, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local
Planning Authority. The EMEP shall include:
· 
A plan showing habitat protection zones.
· 
Details of any precautionary method statements for protected
species.
· 
Details of a sensitive lighting strategy.
· 
Details of wildlife friendly landscaping within curtilage of
private dwellings (must include native tree and hedge planting,
flowering lawns, planting within 6-10m of the watercourse to be in
alignment with EA 3D buffer models (avoiding any direct discharge
into the neighbouring watercourse), rain gardens, and should
include nature-based solutions to grey water management.
· 
Details, specification and location of hedgehog highway within all
lengths of closed panel fence boundaries.
· 
Details, specification and locations of wildlife friendly curb and
drain treatments.
· 
Details, specification and location of the following species
enhancements incorporated into structures across the site:
a) 2 Integrated bird
boxes
b) 2 Integrated bat
boxes
c) 1 to 2 bee/insect
bricks per dwelling
d) 1
hibernaculum
 
The EMEP shall be
implemented in strict accordance with the approved plan. All
features shall be installed during construction and retained as
such thereafter.
 
Reason: In the
interest of nature conservation and to accord with Policy S60 of
the Central Lincolnshire Local Plan (Adopted 2023), NPPF and draft
Local Nature Recovery Strategy.
 
7. 
Any application for the approval of reserved matters relating to
scale and appearance, shall be accompanied by an Energy Statement
to accord with the requirements of policies S6 and S7 of the
Central Lincolnshire Local Plan (Adopted 2023). The statement shall
include a phasing scheme for the development, as well as the
process for verifying that the completed houses have met the energy
efficiency targets as set out within the approved Energy Statement.
Development shall thereafter proceed only in accordance with the
agreed Energy Statement, unless otherwise agreed in writing.
 
Reason: In order to ensure
efficient buildings and reduce energy consumption, in accordance
with Policies S6 and S7 of the Central Lincolnshire Local Plan
(Adopted 2023).
 
8. 
Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning
(General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (or any Order
revoking and re enacting that Order with or without modification)
no domestic oil tanks or domestic gas tanks shall be placed within
the curtilage of the dwelling(s) hereby approved.
 
Reason: In the interests of
energy efficiency to accord with Policies S6 and S7 of the Central
Lincolnshire Local Plan (Adopted 2023).
 
9. 
No works or development shall take place until a scheme for
protection of the retained trees/hedgerows (Section 5.5 BS5837 -
2012 - Tree Protection Plan) has been submitted and agreed in
writing by the Local Planning Authority. This scheme shall
include:
(a) A plan showing details
and positions of the ground protection areas.
(b) Details and position of
protection barriers. Protection barriers should be erected prior to
each construction phase commencing and shall remain in place, and
undamaged for the duration of that phase - these to be retained and
maintained until all equipment, machinery and surplus materials
have been removed from the site.
(c) Details and position of
underground service runs and working methods employed should these
runs be within the designated root protection area of any retained
tree/hedgerow on or adjacent to the application site.
(d) Details of special
engineering required to accommodate the protection of retained
tree/hedgerows e.g. in connection with foundations, bridging, water
features and surfacing.
(e) Details of working
methods to be employed for the installation of drives and paths
within the root protection areas of any retained tree/hedgerow on
or adjacent to the application site.
(f) Details of working
methods to be employed with the demolition of buildings, structures
and surfacing within or adjacent to the root protection areas of
any retained tree/hedgerow on or adjacent to the application
site.
(g) Details of any
scaffolding erection with the root protection areas.
(h) Details of timing for the
various phases of works or development in the context of the
tree/hedgerow protection measures.
(i) Details of any proposed
changes of ground level within the root protection area as defined
to the application site.
Reason: To ensure the retention
of features which are important to the character and amenity of the
surrounding area to accord with Policy S66 of the Central
Lincolnshire Local Plan (Adopted 2023).
 
10.Prohibited activities:
 
In this condition "retained
tree" means an existing tree which is to be retained in accordance
with the approved plans and particulars:
(a) No fires to be lit on
site within 10 metres of the nearest point of the canopy of any
retained tree on or adjacent to the proposal site. Page 50
Official
(b) No equipment, signage,
fencing etc shall be attached to or be supported by any retained
tree on or adjacent to the application site.
(c) No temporary access
within designated Root Protection Areas without the prior written
approval of the district planning authority,
(d) No mixing of cement,
dispensing of fuels or chemicals within 10 metres of the tree stem
of any retained tree on or adjacent to the application site.
(e) No soakaways to be routed
within the Root Protections Areas or any retained tree on or
adjacent to the application site. (f) No stripping of topsoils,
excavations or changing of levels to occur within the Root
Protection Areas of any retained tree on or adjacent to the
application site.
(g) No topsoil, building
materials or other to be stored within the Root Protection Areas of
any retained tree on or adjacent to the application site.
(h) No alterations or
variations of the approved works or tree protection schemes shall
be carried out without the prior written approval of the district
planning authority.
 
Reason: To ensure the retention
of trees which are important to the character and amenity of the
surrounding area to accord with Policy S66 of the Central
Lincolnshire Local Plan (Adopted 2023).
 
11.No development or site
clearance/preparation shall take place unless and until the
applicant, or their agents or successors in title, has secured the
implementation of an agreed written specification that sets out a
programme of work to mitigate the impact of construction to known
archaeological remains. The specification shall be submitted to and
approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The programme
of work shall be carried out strictly in accordance with the
approved specification.
 
Reason: To ensure that
archaeological remains are preserved in situ or investigated and
recorded as appropriate and to ensure that the information is made
available, in accordance with Policy S57 of the Central
Lincolnshire Local Plan (Adopted 2023).
 
12.Notwithstanding the provisions
of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development)
(England) Order 2015 (or any Order revoking and re enacting that
Order with or without modification):
(a) No external alterations
shall be carried out to the dwellings (b) No extensions shall be
carried out to the dwellings
(c) No garages or
outbuildings incidental to the enjoyment of the dwelling/s shall be
erected within the curtilage of the dwellings Official Page 51
(d) No vehicle standing space
or hard standing shall be provided within the curtilage of the
dwellings
(e) No gates, walls, fences
or other structures shall be erected along any boundary to the
curtilage of the dwellings
(f) No means of vehicular
access shall be constructed to the curtilage of the dwellings
(g) No windows or dormer
windows shall be added to the dwellings other than those expressly
authorised by this permission, unless planning permission for such
development has been granted by the Local Planning Authority.
 
Reason: The Local Planning
Authority would wish to consider the potential impacts of such
works in relation to matters of flood risk, drainage and visual
amenity in accordance with Policies S21 and S53 of the Central
Lincolnshire Local Plan (Adopted 2023).
 
13.The dwelling/s hereby approved
shall be constructed to ensure that the consumption of wholesome
water by persons occupying the dwelling/s is in accordance with the
Building Regulations Approved Document G, Requirement G2/Regulation
36 Optional Technical Requirement of 110 litres per person per
day.
 
Reason: To minimise impacts on
the water environment and to accord with Optional Technical Housing
Standards to accord with Policies S12 and S53 of the Central
Lincolnshire Local Plan (Adopted 2023).
 
14.The development hereby permitted
shall not be carried out except in complete accordance with the
details shown on the approved plans, listed below on this decision
notice.
 
Reason: To ensure that the
development takes place in accordance with the approved
details.

content:
The Local Plans Manager presented the 2025/26
Central Lincolnshire Joint Strategic Planning Committee Annual
report.
 
The report included a summary of the
Committee’s progress, a forward look at the work for 2026/27,
and a financial and staffing overview.
 
During 2025/26 the Committee had considered
items including a vision for the Central Lincolnshire
Authority-wide Design Code, a wider update on that work, as well as
proposals for the review of the Central Lincolnshire Local Plan and
principles for undertaking the Plan review.
 
The Committee had approved the commencement of
work on the Local Plan, and the Local Plans Team had started work
on preparing and updating the evidence base for the review.
 
The Team were also implementing the
‘Integrated Mapping and Engagement System’ funded by
the Government’s Proptech grant
programme, which involved developing tools to deliver efficiencies
in plan-making. Due to changes from Government, there was no longer
a requirement for Authority-Wide Design Codes to be produced for
Local Planning Authorities. The Spatial Development Strategy was
now the responsibility of the Greater Lincolnshire County Combined
Authority (GLCCA) and evidence sharing to ensure consistency would
be explored. 
 
In response to questions from Members, the
Local Plans Manager advised that:
· 
Currently there was no set timetable for the Spatial Development
Strategy, however it was anticipated that it would progress quickly
once it started.
· 
The timetable and notifications for the Local Plan would start
before the end of the year.
· 
Concerns around the challenges in meeting the Government’s
housing targets and impacts on quality were shared, and the Local
Plan would continue to strive for design quality with site specific
polices and early engagement with Developers.
· 
Rising construction costs were also a concern and the requirement
for viability assessments were part of the Local Plan.
· 
Lincolnshire County Council’s Minerals and Waste Plan was
currently out for consultation and that document incorporated the
anticipated demand for materials across the County. The impact of
Nationally Significant Infrastructure Projects (NSIPs) coming
forward on supply and demand for materials was not yet clear and
would form part of the County’s Minerals and Waste Plan.
· 
Consultants were often commissioned to undertake viability
assessments and viability levels were set at the Local Plan level
to reduce the need at planning application level. Viability
assessments on individual cases were not usually necessary unless
there was a specific reason for it.
· 
Viability options would be brought back to the Committee and the
best ways to ensure development was delivered would be needed going
forward.
 
Due to concerns about the impact on materials
from NSIPs, it was requested that the Local Plans Manager raise
these observations with Lincolnshire County Council.
 
Members thanked the Local Plans Manager and
his team for the report.
 
Vote:
 
Unanimous
 
RESOLVED:
 
That the 2025/26 Annual report was approved as
a fair summary of activity of the Central Lincolnshire Joint
Strategic Planning Committee and, it was recommended that it be
circulated to each of the respective Partner Authorities.
topline: The Central Lincolnshire Joint Strategic Planning Committee has decided to approve the 2025/26 Annual report and recommendations for the review of the Local Plan.

content:
The Local Plans Manager presented the Central
Lincolnshire Budget Update report, which contained the latest Local
Plan budget position, the outturn for 2025/26, the approved budget
for 2026/27, and the proposed contribution level to be sought from
each Partner Authority.
 
Appendix 1 to the report detailed the 2025/26
expected and actual outturn expenditure. Appendix 2 to the report
detailed the approved and projected budget. Appendix 3 to the
report detailed the 2027/28 – 2029/30 budget provisions.
 
The Committee noted that:
· 
due to consultancy support not being procured in 2025/26 and the
receipt of Government funding through Proptech for software costs,
that there was an underspend of £107,505.
· 
Additional funding of £30,000 from Proptech had also been
secured for the carbon assessment tool.
· 
At the end of 2025/26 the reserves balance was £354,850.
· 
The net expenditure was higher than anticipated at £666,610,
due to increased consultancy costs. This was because support for
the Local Plan review was included within the current year, rather
than spread across last year and this year.
· 
The reserve balance at the end of the financial year was expected
to be £126,382.
· 
Contributions of £138,000 would be sought from each of the
Central Lincolnshire District Councils for 2027/28 and this was
slightly lower than projected in the approved 2024 budget.
· 
The partnership still represented value for money.
 
In response to questions from Members of the
Committee the Local Plans Manager advised that:
· 
In 2024 the Committee approved the reserves balance of
£80,000 to enable flexibility and a contingency within the
year for additional costs.
 
Vote:
 
Unanimous
 
RESOLVED:
 
That the Committee noted the outturn for
2025/26 and the current budget forecast for 2026/27-2029/30
including the contribution level of £138,000 to be requested
from each of the Central Lincolnshire District Councils for the
2027/28 fiscal year.
topline: The Local Plans Manager has decided to request each Central Lincolnshire District Council to contribute £138,000 for the 2027/28 fiscal year.

Location:


352 Brant Road and Land to the West of Brant
Road, Waddington




Applicant:


Lindum Group Limited




Agent:


Freeths LLP




Reason
for Committee Consideration:


Officer referral through section 7.02 of the
NKDC constitution owing to the application raising locally
significant policy issues which are of significant public
interest.




 
Councillor Pennell
stated for openness and transparency purposes that the registered
public speaker from Waddington Parish Council (Councillor
Gallagher) was known to some Members of the Committee, as he had
previously been a District Councillor.
 
Councillor Pennell
also stated for openness and transparency purposes that he had been
present at Waddington Parish Council meetings when registered
speaker’s Councillor Dyer and Councillor Gallagher had been
present and the application was discussed. However, he had not
expressed an opinion and had an open mind to consider the
application. 
 
Councillor
Carrington declared an Other Registrable Interest as a Member of
Lincolnshire County Council, who were a consultee on this
application. 
 
The Development Manager presented the
application using maps, plans and photographs to demonstrate the
location and character of the site, as well as the material issues
identified in the agenda report. He also drew Members’
attention to the relevant national and local planning policies.
 
Since the publication of the agenda two
further representations raising objections to the application had
been received from Mr S Clark of 322 Brant Road and Mr S Fuller of
12 Belvoir Close. These representations related to similar comments
that had already been submitted and summarised within the agenda in
terms of:
· 
Historic and ongoing drainage matters. 
· 
Flood risk concerns to existing properties in the surrounding
area.
· 
The proposed development adding to the existing flooding
issues.
· 
Another new development in close proximity to the site causing
off-site issues.
· 
Dispute that the application site was disused, underused or not in
agricultural use. 
· 
The application placing undue strain on local services.
 
The Committee also noted that there were some
errors within paragraphs 7 to 9 of the Officer report regarding
references to the Drainage Strategy, community involvement and the
Longhurst Group, as this information related to the 2021
application and not the current proposal before Members.
 
The Development Manager advised the Committee
that if the application was approved it was also now recommended
that an additional planning condition be included to require three
bin collection points (shown on the revised site layout plan) to
serve the private drive on the western site boundary, which would
be installed prior to first occupation of those dwellings and then
retained. 
 
The proposal sought to demolish 352 Brant Road
and then utilise part of the existing access to this property. The
application was an ‘exception’ site under Policy S4
which aimed to provide 51 affordable dwellings. There would be a
range of 2, 3 and 4 bed house types and 4 x 1-bedroom flats, as
well as the provision of useable greenspace to include a local area
of play. Construction of estate roads, private drives and
associated infrastructure also formed part of the proposals.
 
The key issues of the application were:
· 
The Principle of Development.
· 
Landscape impact, design and visual amenity considerations.
· 
Residential amenity.
· 
Energy efficiency.
· 
Flood risk and drainage.
· 
Parking and highways safety.
· 
The natural environment – landscaping, trees, ecology and
biodiversity net gain.
· 
Other issues – infrastructure.
 
172 written representations received prior to
the agenda publication raising objection/concern to the scheme were
summarised within the agenda report. 
 
The Officer assessment was also contained
within the agenda with the recommendation that Authority to Deal be
given to Officers to approve under delegated powers upon completion
of a Section 106 Planning Agreement, subject to Planning Conditions
and the additional bin storage Condition.
 
The meeting then adjourned to allow the
registered speakers to address the meeting. Councillor Dyer spoke
as an Objector, Councillor Gallagher spoke on behalf of Waddington
Parish Council and Mark Bassett spoke on behalf of the Applicant.
All speakers answered questions from Members of the Committee.
 
There were no Local Ward Members/Strong
Community Advocates registered to speak and the meeting then
resumed formal session.
 
Members debated the application in detail,
considering the Officer’s report, presentation and statements
from the registered public speakers. During the debate, several
Members of the Committee raised concerns about the proposal
including:
· 
Acknowledging the level of local objection to the scheme from
residents.
· 
The impacts on the Green Wedge and the tension between the
Commentary document (GWSBR 2016) and Policy (adopted with
modifications in 2023) in terms of preventing the merging of
settlements.
· 
The implications of Policy S63 that planning permission should not
be granted for any form of development unless (a) the development
was not contrary or detrimental to the various functions set out in
the report and (b) it was essential that the proposed development
was located within the Green Wedge. It was considered that this had
not been demonstrated but that this must then be balanced against
other planning factors in favour of the scheme.
· 
Historical flooding issues within the area and the impact that the
application would have on future flood risk and drainage
matters.
· 
The capacity and capability of the Water Recycling Centre to
accommodate further pressures.
· 
The suitability and longevity of the surface water drainage scheme
for this development and the sustainability over time of the
underground crate system.
· 
Future maintenance and responsibility for the surface water
drainage scheme including the ditch that would receive flows from
the lagoon and underground storage system. Further flood risk and
drainage mitigation measures for the dwellings on this site
including raised floor levels for greater protection for
residents.
· 
Safety at the crossing points at Brant Road, particularly for
children crossing the road to go to school.
· 
Whether this was the best use of the land and alternative sites for
this development.
· 
The flood risk for the Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) provision area
and whether suitable species would be selected based on the flood
risk to the BNG area.
· 
Maintenance and safety of the play area and the attenuation pond
including provision of fencing.
 
However, during the discussion of this
application other Members of the Committee considered that:
· 
The assumption should be that the relevant authorities and bodies
would carry out their specific legal duties and responsibilities
for water management and maintenance.
· 
Whilst there was concern around local flood risk, many of the
concerns about historical flooding matters needed to be separated
from the Committee’s consideration of this application, as
the Environment Agency (EA) flood zone mapping showed that the
residential part of the site was in Flood Zone 1.
· 
If the application was approved, then under Condition 18 the final
site levels would be reassessed and final finished floor levels
would be set.
· 
Whether there was scope for further and increased mitigation
measures for flood risk within Condition 24 (re-verification of the
technical calculations and construction level drawings of all the
drainage assets to enable Officers and relevant consultees to
assess final details and avoid drainage issues further down the
line).
· 
The importance of the maintenance and responsibility for all
drainage assets including the ditch being included within Condition
24 (specific details of the maintenance cycle and
responsibility).
· 
As Anglian Water and the EA had confirmed that the Waste Recycling
Centre had capacity to deal with foul water flows then the
Committee could not refuse the application on those grounds, as
there was no evidence that it could not accept those
flows. 
· 
Design, density, amenity and highways matters were addressed and
acceptable.
· 
There was not a sustainable planning reason to refuse the
application.
 
In response to questions from the Committee,
the Development Manager advised that:
· 
Drone images of flooding in Waddington in 2024 that did not reach
the application site, were submitted by the Applicant and showed
high water levels at that point in time. It was not reflective of
the whole year or past or present trends.
· 
The EA flood zone maps were regularly reviewed and updated, and
flood zones could and did change. However, decisions had to be made
using the current flood zone mapping for the site. Climate Change
projections were also incorporated into the EA flood maps and
associated updates.
· 
Officers undertook the Policy assessment against the EA national
level flood mapping analysis, and the Committee were being asked to
determine the application in line with the most up to date EA flood
mapping information.
· 
Lincolnshire County Council - Highways had not requested any
signalised or non-signalised pedestrian crossing for this scheme
across Brant Road. The provisions requested were appropriate for
the size and scale of the proposed development and the location of
facilities on the opposite side of the road.
· 
Clarification on the Surface Water Drainage plan for the site
including how the underground crate storage system would work in
tandem with the balancing pond. 
· 
There had been no objections raised by the Internal Drainage Board
(IDB) regarding surface water run-off. A surface water drainage
plan was in place and there would be two attenuation ponds.
· 
The surface water drainage measures on and off site would have
capabilities to deal with 1 in 100 year plus a 40% climate change
events. There were riparian owner responsibilities in place for
maintenance of the drainage ditch off site and the IDB also had
responsibilities for their water course.
· 
No objections (subject to Conditions) had been raised by
Lincolnshire County Council (LCC) as the Lead Local Flood Authority
to the proposed scheme. Condition 24 (requested by LCC) required
the surface water drainage scheme (including the crate system) to
be maintained and managed over the lifetime of the development.
· 
Due to the infiltration levels on the site, there was a combination
of piping, use of balancing ponds and crates proposed. The site was
also within flood zone 1 and therefore there was no requirement for
raised floor levels or other mitigation measures to address
residual flood risk impacts. 
· 
It was anticipated that the attenuation basins would be adopted by
LCC and that the crate system would come under a management company
or another body. 
· 
There was an under provision of Affordable Homes in Waddington and
the Committee could not give any planning weight to alternative
sites that may be coming through or that were available. The
application had to be determined on its merits 
· 
The BNG provision for this site had been assessed as suitable and
this was an area that would be dealt with after the decision had
been made on the application.
· 
The IDB’s and the EA had different specific duties and
responsibilities for water management and maintenance of assets,
and no concerns had been raised about breaks in ownership or
third-party liabilities to accommodate the flows from this
development. 
· 
The wording of Condition 18 (levels of all site structures and
flood risk related) could be expanded to include that the site
levels would be informed by the surface water drainage scheme and
the attenuation measures in Condition 24.
· 
Condition 24 (detailed drainage scheme) would not be discharged
without the consent of the statutory consultees who would need to
be fully satisfied with the required technical calculations and
information that was submitted. Construction level drawings would
not necessarily add value or clarity and the concern was to the
lack of precision in the wording of the condition if additional
text was included to require ‘construction level
plans’.
· 
The final bullet point of Condition 24 could be expanded to include
all drainage assets including the connection to the
watercourse.
· 
There was no surface water storage associated with the
children’s play area. There was provision within the planning
condition to include a small fence if it was deemed appropriate
further down the line, and it did not restrict access for
maintenance.  Condition 17 related to
maintenance of the play area and this was usually offered to the
Parish Council in the first instance or alternatively a management
company would be responsible. It was confirmed that the District
Council would be unlikely to adopt and maintain the area.
· 
As the site was within flood zone 1 and not at risk of surface
water or river flooding, it would not be reasonable to add
additional flood risk mitigations to the Conditions, as there was
no justification. There was also no planning policy reason or
identified need in the flood risk assessment. 
 
It was therefore proposed and seconded that
planning permission be granted in line with the Officer
recommendation and that Authority to Deal be given to Officers to
approve under delegated powers upon the completion of a Section 106
Planning Agreement and Planning Conditions (including the
additional bin storage Condition and the amendments to Condition 18
and Condition 24).

run-off from the highway.
 
The approved scheme shall be
implemented in full and in accordance with the approved timetable
of works.
 
Reason: To incorporate active
travel infrastructure as part of the design of the scheme by
providing safe and adequate pedestrian access to the development,
without increasing flood risk to the highway and adjacent land and
property.
 
21.Prior to first occupation on
site further details relating to the vehicular access to the public
highway, including materials, specification of works and
construction method shall be submitted to the Local Planning
Authority for approval. The approved details shall be implemented
on site before the development is first occupied and thereafter
retained at all times.
 
Reason: In the interests of
safety of the users of the public highway and the safety of the
users of the site.
 
22.Before any dwelling is occupied,
all of that part of the estate road and associated footways that
forms the junction with the main road and which will be constructed
within the limits of the existing highway, shall be laid out and
constructed to finished surface levels in accordance with details
to be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning
Authority.
 
Reason: In the interests of
safety, to avoid the creation of pedestrian trip hazards within the
public highway from surfacing materials, manholes and gullies that
may otherwise remain for an extended period at dissimilar, interim
construction levels.
 
23.No development (with the
exception of the demolition of 352 Brant Road) shall commence until
an Estate Road Phasing and Completion Plan has been submitted to
and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan
shall set out how the construction of the development will be
phased and standards to which the estate roads on each phase will
be completed during the construction period of the development.
 
Reason: To ensure that a safe
and suitable standard of vehicular and pedestrian access is
provided for residents throughout the construction period of the
development.
 
24.No development (with the
exception of the demolition of 352 Brant Road) shall commence until
a surface water drainage scheme has been submitted to and approved
in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
 
The scheme shall:
· 
be based on verified groundwater levels and seasonal variations, as
evidenced through on-site monitoring conducted over a six-month
winter period;
· 
be based on sustainable drainage principles and an assessment of
the hydrological and hydrogeological context of the
development;
· 
provide flood exceedance routing for storm event greater than 1 in
100 year;
· 
provide details of how run-off will be safely conveyed and
attenuated during storms up to and including the 1 in 100 year
critical storm event, with an allowance for climate change, from
all hard surfaced areas within the development into the existing
local drainage infrastructure and watercourse system without
exceeding the run-off rate for the undeveloped site;
· 
provide attenuation details and discharge rates which shall be
restricted an agreed amount of litres per second;
· 
provide details of the timetable for and any phasing of
implementation for the drainage scheme; and
· 
provide details of how all surface water drainage
components/assets comprised in the scheme, including the receiving
watercourse, shall be maintained and managed
over the lifetime of the development, including any arrangements
for adoption by any public body or Statutory Undertaker and any
other arrangements required to secure the operation of the drainage
system throughout its lifetime.
 
No dwelling/ no part of the
development shall be occupied until
the approved scheme has been
completed or provided on the
site in accordance with the approved
phasing.
 
The approved scheme shall be retained
and maintained in full,
in accordance with the approved
details.
 
Reason: To ensure that the permitted
development is
adequately drained without creating
or increasing flood risk to
land or property adjacent to, or
downstream of, or upstream of,
the permitted development.
 
25.Before the first occupation of
plots 15, 29 and 30 hereby permitted the windows at the first floor
side elevation; shall be fitted with obscure glazing, to a minimum
of level 3 obscuration and shall be permanently retained in that
condition thereafter.
 
Reason: To safeguard the
privacy and amenity of the occupiers of adjacent properties to
accord with Policy S53 of the Central Lincolnshire Local Plan
(adopted 2023).
 
26.Notwithstanding the provisions
of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development)
(England) Order 2015 (or any Order revoking and re enacting that
Order with or without modification) no domestic oil tanks or
domestic gas tanks shall be placed within the curtilage of the
dwelling(s) herby approved.
 
Reason: In the interests of
energy efficiency to accord with Policies S6 and S7 of the Central
Lincolnshire Local Plan (adopted 2023).
 
27.Before any part of the
development hereby permitted is occupied/brought into use, a
verification report confirming that remedial works have been
completed shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by
the Local Planning Authority. The report shall have been submitted
in accordance with the ‘Additional Investigation and
Remediation Strategy’ prepared by Delta Simmons. The report
shall include:
 
i. A complete record of
remediation activities, and data collected as identified in the
remediation scheme, to support compliance with agreed remediation
objectives;
ii. As built drawings of the
implemented scheme;
iii. Photographs of the
remediation works in progress; and
iv. Certificates
demonstrating that imported and/or material left in situ is free
from contamination.
 
The scheme of remediation
shall thereafter be maintained in accordance with the approved
scheme.
 
Reason: Previous activities
associated with this site may have caused, or had the potential to
cause, land contamination and to ensure that the proposed site
investigations and remediation will not cause pollution in the
interests of the amenities of the future residents and users of the
development to accord with Policies S53 and S56 of the Central
Lincolnshire Local Plan (adopted 2023).
 
28.The Bin stores shown on the
submitted Site Plan ref. JV_175_02 Rev F shall be implemented prior
to first occupation of the associated properties and thereafter
retained for the lifetime of the development.
 
Reason: For the avoidance of
doubt and to ensure that sufficient bin stores are provided for
occupants of respective properties to accord with Policy S53 of the
Central Lincolnshire Local Plan (adopted 2023).
 
29.The development hereby permitted
shall not be carried out except in complete accordance with the
details shown on the approved plans, listed below on this decision
notice. 
 
Reason: To ensure that the
development takes place in accordance with the approved
details.

Application No. and Type:


26/0114/FUL




Proposal:


Change of use to class E(g) (Workshops),
including external alterations (retrospective)




Location:


North And South Barns, West of Brant Lodge
Stragglethorpe LN5 0QZ




Applicant:


EA & SJ Ward




Agent:


George Machin, Grace Machin Planning &
Property




Reason
for Committee Consideration:


This application has been referred back to Committee to specifically consider
the matter relating to Biodiversity Net Gain and the application of
Policy S61 of the Central Lincolnshire Local Plan further to a
resolution to approve the application by Planning Committee on 7th
April 2026.




 
Using photographs and plans, the Principal
Planning Officer presented the application which had been approved
by the Planning Committee at their meeting on Tuesday
7th April 2026. The application was for the change of
use of two buildings to a Class E(g) Use and associated conversion
works.
 
The purpose of the report before the Committee
was to update Members on the comments from the Principal Ecology
and Wildlife Officer, the application of planning policy in
relation to Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) and the implications on the
Planning Conditions. All other matters were unchanged from the
report considered by Members in April and as recorded in the
published minutes.
 
Following the Planning Committee meeting in
April, a revised Location Plan had been submitted by the Applicant
and in response to that comments were received from the Principal
Ecology and Wildlife Officer.
 
The Principal Planning Officer advised that
there had also been an error in April’s Committee report, as
it stated that the site was exempt from mandatory BNG due to
permitted development rights. However, Policy S61 should have been
applied to the proposal, and the Applicant had agreed to provide
ten trees which would offset the loss and provide the necessary BNG
requirement for this site.
 
The only matters for consideration and debate
by the Committee were the key issues of Biodiversity Net Gain and
Landscaping and the additional two Planning Conditions regarding
planting details and the maintenance period. 
 
11 objections and 3 letters of support had
been received but these did not contain any new issues that had not
been raised as part of the previous representations, which were
detailed within the agenda.
 
The Officer assessment was contained within
the agenda with the recommendation that two additional Conditions
(8 and 9) be included with the overall Planning Conditions approved
by the Committee on Tuesday 7th April 2026.
 
There were no registered public speakers or
Local Ward Members/Strong Community Advocates.
 
Considering the Officer’s report and
presentation, Members were content with the reasoning and inclusion
of the additional Planning Conditions to address matters of
BNG.
 
It was therefore proposed and seconded that
the two new Planning Conditions (8 and 9) detailed within the
agenda be approved and included with the Conditions that were
approved at the Planning Committee meeting on Tuesday
7th April 2026. The previous Condition 8 would become
Condition 10.
 
Vote:
 
Unanimous
 
RESOLVED:
 
That the two new Planning Conditions (8 and 9)
be approved and included with the Conditions that were approved at
the Planning Committee meeting on Tuesday 7th April
2026. The previous Condition 8 would become Condition 10.
 
Conditions:
 
1. 
Within 6 weeks of the date of this consent, a scheme for the
mitigation of light pollution, to include cowling around the lights
shown on Drawing titled ‘Plans and Elevation as converted
South Barn’ shall be submitted for approval in writing by the
Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall include details of the
timing of the lighting relative to the operational hours specified
in Condition 4. The approved scheme shall be implemented in full
within 8 weeks of the date of that approval and retained
thereafter. No external lighting other than that approved as part
of this permission shall be installed on the buildings or sited
within its curtilage.
 
Reason: In the interests of the
visual amenity of the area, to protect the amenity of the occupiers
of nearby residential properties, and to preserve the significance
of the Listed Official Building to accord with policies S53 and S57
of the Central Lincolnshire Local Plan (adopted 2023).
 
2. 
Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning
(General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 as amended and
the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as
amended), the units hereby permitted shall be occupied only for a
use falling within Use Class E(g) and for no other purpose without
the express permission of the Local Planning Authority.
 
Reason: In the interests of the
visual amenity of the area, to protect the amenity of the occupiers
of nearby residential properties, and to preserve the significance
of the Listed Building to accord with policies S53 and S57 of the
Central Lincolnshire Local Plan (adopted 2023).
 
3. 
Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning
(General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended),
or any Order revoking and re enacting
that Order with or without modification, no development of the
types described in Schedule 2, Part 7, Class A shall be carried out
on North Barn or South Barn without the express permission of the
Local Planning Authority.
 
Reason: In the interests of the
visual amenity of the area, to protect the amenity of the occupiers
of nearby residential properties, and to preserve the significance
of the Listed Building to accord with policies S53 and S57 of the
Central Lincolnshire Local Plan (adopted 2023).
 
4. 
No operations shall occur, and no visitors, deliveries, or
collections shall access the site, outside the following hours:
07:30 to 19:00 Monday- Friday, 08:00 to 13:00 on Saturdays, and at
no time Sundays, Bank or Public Holidays.
 
Reason: To prevent noise and
disturbance to the occupiers of nearby residential properties and
to preserve the significance of the Listed Building to accord with
policies S53 and S57 of the Central Lincolnshire Local Plan
(adopted 2023).
 
5. 
No processes, including manufacture and maintenance, or any
activity except loading and unloading associated with the use
hereby approved shall take place on any part of land outside of the
building/s.
 
Reason: To prevent noise and
disturbance to the occupiers of nearby residential properties to
accord with policy S53 of the Central Lincolnshire Local Plan
(adopted 2023).
 
6. 
The rating level of noise emitted from any plant and equipment on
site shall not exceed the existing background level by more than
+5dB(A) at any time. The noise levels shall be taken at the nearest
noise sensitive premises. The measurements and assessments shall be
made in accordance with BS4142:2014.
 
No external plant or
machinery shall be installed or used without the express permission
of the Local Planning Authority.
 
Reason: In the interests of
residential amenity to accord with Policy S53 of the Central
Lincolnshire Local Plan (adopted 2023).
 
7. 
Within 6 weeks of the date of this permission a scheme (with
specifications, a timetable for implementation, and supported by an
appropriately scaled plan) for the provision of ecological habitat
enhancements including bird and bat boxes and roosting features
shall have been submitted for approval in writing by the Local
Planning Authority. The approved scheme shall be implemented in
full within 8 weeks of the date of that approval and retained
thereafter.
 
Reason: In the interest of
achieving long term biodiversity gains to accord with Policies S60
and S61 of the Central Lincolnshire Local Plan (adopted 2023).
 
 
8. 
Within 6 weeks of the date of this permission a scheme for the
provision of landscaping shall be submitted for approval in writing
by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall include the
provision of at least 10 native species trees and including details
of the proposed location, species, size and the oversailing
habitat. The scheme shall be implemented in full before the end of
the next planting season and retained in full for at least 30
years.
 
Reason: In the interest of
achieving long term biodiversity gains to accord with Policies S60
and S61 of the Central Lincolnshire Local Plan (adopted 2023).
 
9. 
Within 6 weeks of the date of this permission a scheme for the
management and maintenance of the landscaping scheme required by
condition 8 above shall be submitted for approval in writing by the
Local Planning Authority. Such a scheme shall include provision of
the regular maintenance of trees, details of adaptive management
and remedial measures to account for any shortfall in biodiversity
gain and/or loss of trees within that time
period, details of the person(s) responsible for the
implementation of the scheme, and provision for 5 yearly reporting
of the scheme. The approved scheme shall take effect following the
completion of the approved landscaping scheme and shall remain in
effect for a period of at least 30 years.
 
Reason: In the interest of
achieving long term biodiversity gains to accord with Policies S60
and S61 of the Central Lincolnshire Local Plan (adopted 2023).
 
10.The development hereby permitted
shall not be carried out except in complete accordance with the
details shown on the approved plans, listed below on this decision
notice.
 
Reason: To ensure that the
development takes place in accordance with the approved
details.
topline: The Planning Committee has decided to approve the change of use to workshops at North and South Barns, with additional Planning Conditions to address Biodiversity Net Gain and landscaping concerns.

content:
Application No. and Type:


23/1462/OUT Outline Application




Proposal:


Erection of up to 17 no. dwellings and
formulation of new vehicular access from Fen Lane (outline with
access to be considered)




Location:


Land North of Fen Lane, Dunston




Applicant:


AG Property Associates Limited




Agent:


Knights




Reason
for Committee Consideration:


Application is being reported to committee to
update Members on a modification made to the Environment
Agency’s Flood Maps on 25th March 2025 which affects the
site.




 
Using photographs and plans, the Development
Manager presented a report relating to an application that had been
approved by the Planning Committee on Tuesday 8th
October 2024. The application was for outline planning permission
for the erection of up to 17 dwellings, with the formation of a new
vehicular access from Fen Lane (all other matters - appearance,
landscaping, layout and scale had been reserved for later detailed
approval).
 
The Committee were being updated on changes to
the Environment Agency’s (EA) Flood Zone mapping system that
took place in March 2025, which had elevated the flood risk status
of the application site from Flood Zone 1 to a hybrid of Flood
Zones 1, 2 and 3, with areas of Flood Zones 2 and 3 running
centrally through the site. As the Section 106 Agreement was not
complete at the time the site’s flood risk status changed
then the application remained live and therefore had to be
determined in line with latest available technical evidence and
constraint mapping. The Applicant had also submitted additional
information to address the elevated flood risk in consultation with
the EA.
 
30 representations in relation to the original
planning application were summarised within the agenda. However no
additional comments were received from members of the public in
relation to the update given that re-consultation was not carried
out.
 
The Officer assessment was contained within
the agenda with the recommendation that Authority to Deal be
approved subject to the completion of a Section 106 Agreement and
an amendment to Condition 19 (all other Conditions remained
unchanged and as set out in the 8th October 2024
Committee report).
 
There were no registered public speakers or
Local Ward Members/Strong Community Advocates.
 
Members then discussed the application,
considering the Officer’s report and presentation. During the
debate, Members raised the following points including:
· 
The impact of the flood zone changes on the Central Lincolnshire
Local Plan (CLLP) allocation of the site and whether this still
carried significant planning weight in light of the flood zone
changes.
· 
Whether it would be reasonable to include flood resilient
construction techniques to be used within amended Condition 19.
· 
The Applicant had responded to the EA flood mapping change through
their flood risk assessment and associated flood modelling and
although it was an unusual case, evidence had been provided by the
EA and the Applicant that the site was at low risk of flooding and
there were mitigation measures proposed. 
· 
The significant planning weight of the site allocation through the
CLLP with reference to how the flood risk sequential test should be
considered for this site.
 
In response to questions from the Committee,
the Development Manager advised that:
· 
Various technical information including the EA’s flood
mapping system were used to determine allocation of sites when the
2023 CLLP was in preparation.

It was the Officer’s view that
the site’s CLLP allocation still carried significant weight
in the context of the flood risk sequential test and it was noted
that the Local Plan policy does reference an element of surface
water risk to the site requiring mitigation, notwithstanding the
subsequent change to flood mapping.
The Applicant’s flood risk
assessment response to the flood zone changes demonstrated that the
site would be safe from flooding, as sufficient mitigation measures
were proposed.
The exception test in terms of wider
benefits had also been satisfied in relation to this site through
delivery of affordable housing, BNG and accommodating the existing
right of way through the indicative scheme design.
The EA had raised no objections to
the proposal subject to Conditions requiring mitigation measures
being implemented and development being a minimum of 2 stories in
height.
A non-allocated site in Flood Zones
2 or 3 would have been scrutinised in terms of other site options.
The allocated nature of the site gave it significant planning
weight in the application of the sequential test; however this
would not have engaged had the site been ‘windfall’
(non-allocated).
It would not be unreasonable to
further amend Condition 19 to include that flood resilient
construction techniques be used and section 5.4 of the Flood Risk
Assessment stated that the development should incorporate flood
resilient and resistant measures.
In response to the EA flood mapping
change, the latest Flood Risk Assessment from the Applicant
recommended flood resilient measures.
Anglian Water had confirmed that
they were upgrading the Metheringham Waste Recycling Centre between
2025 and 2030 and that it would be able to accommodate foul
drainage from this site. If the outline planning permission was
approved by the Committee, a Reserved matters application would
then be needed to start works and the applications together would
take around 5 years and line up with the Anglian Water upgrade
timescales. In this regard the situation and consultee position on
foul drainage had not altered since the original report to
members.
There were differences between the
EA national modelling and local level mapping and although the
national mapping showed high risk, it was actually at low risk
locally for flooding. 
The Education Authority had made a
request for a £99,000 primary school contribution however
this could not be accommodated mindful of the advanced stage of
Section 106 drafting and that the Education Authority had initially
made a nil request at the point of previous planning committee
consideration. It would be unreasonable to include this additional
request at this advanced stage.

 
It was therefore proposed and seconded that
planning permission be granted in line with the Officer
recommendation and that Authority to Deal be given to Officers to
approve under delegated powers upon the completion of a Section 106
Planning Agreement and amended Planning Condition 19, as well as
the other Planning Conditions approved at the Planning Committee on
Tuesday 8th October 2024. 
 
Vote:
 
For: 9  Against: 0  Abstentions: 1
 
 
RESOLVED:
 
That Authority to deal and approve subject to
the completion of a Section 106 Agreement addressing the following
Heads of Terms and subject to the revised Condition 19 as listed
below and with all other conditions as set out in the
8th October 2024 Committee Report:
 
Section 106 Heads of
Terms:
 
1. Provision of a scheme for 20% affordable
housing as part of the development
2. Payment of a commuted sum of
£10,752.50 towards improved healthcare facilities in the
area, prioritised to Church Walk Surgery in Metheringham and/or the
Tasburgh Lodge Surgery in Woodhall Spa.
 
Condition 19 to be
reworded as below:
 
Revised Condition 19:
 
The development shall be carried out in
accordance with the submitted flood risk assessment undertaken by
aegaea [ref: AEG8657_LN4_NorthKesteven_01b, Issue 5, dated 22 April
2026] and the following mitigation measures it details.
 
· 
Finished floor levels shall be set no lower than stated in the
FRA.
· 
The development shall have at least two storeys.
· 
The flood resistance and resilience measures shall be
implemented as set out at section 5.4

The Committee considered the report which
sought nominations for the Combined Authority ahead of their annual
meeting scheduled to take place on Wednesday 3 June 2026.
 
Nominations were requested from each District
and Borough Council ahead of the meeting and a list was circulated
at the meeting.  It was noted that there
were three contested seats, one for Audit Committee and two for the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee.
 
The uncontested seats were proposed by Cllr
Leyland and seconded by Cllr Brockway to be approved on block, this
was seconded and unanimously agreed.
 
The contested appointments were taken in order
and voted upon as follows:-
 
Audit Committee - Reform Member seat:
Councillor Hasan received 4 votes and
Councillor Jeal received 1 vote and there was 1 Abstention.
 
Councillor Hasan was
appointed as the Member for the Reform Seat on Audit Committee.
 
It was noted that there was a vacant Reform
seat for the substitute Member. 
Councillor Stokes proposed that Councillor Jeal be considered for
the substitute seat, this was seconded and voted upon.  With 5 votes in favour, Councillor Jeal (SKDC)
was appointed to the Reform seat as a substitute member for Audit
Committee.
 
Overview and Scrutiny Committee – Labour
Member seat
Councillor Steptoe received 5 votes,
Councillor Wells received 0 votes and there was 1 Abstention.
 
Councillor Steptoe
(SKDC) was appointed as the Member for the Labour seat on the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee.
 
Overview and Scrutiny Committee –
Liberal Democrat Member seat
Councillor Boles received 4 votes, Councillor
Turner received 2 votes.
 
Councillor Boles
(WLDC) was appointed to the Liberal Democrat seat on the Overview
and Scrutiny Committee.

The District Joint Committee considered the
report which explored an approach to improve the support provided
to non-constituent members on the various GLCCA Executive
Committees (Boards) and other committees.  The report provided different options to
facilitate this support.
 
Following discussion, it was suggested that an
approach should be made in the first instance to the GLCCA to
provide support to the non-constituent members as is provided to
the Constituent members.  In the event that this was not possible, the
Committee were content to support Option D in the report which
sought a single central lead approach and provided a broader
strategic context and policy perspectives.
 
It was also noted that there was an option to
invite newly appointed officers to future meetings of the District
Joint Committee.
 
The Committee
resolved to:
 
1. 
Write to GLCCA to request support for District Council Members
and attendance at briefings.
2. 
Write to GLCCA to invite Officers to DJC meetings to share
information ahead of GLCCA meetings
3. 
Exploration and implementation of Option D was agreed
4. 
Invite the new Director for Strategy and Operations to share
their vision and next steps for the GLCCA by attending a future DJC
meeting.

content:
The Leader proposed the recommendations of the
Executive Board report which sought support for strategies and
wider financial reports which underpinned the budgets for
2026/27.
 
There was specific reference that having
regard to the MHCLG Guidance and in confirming determination
of a 100% second home premium for 2025-26 where a property was
furnished but was not occupied by anyone as their sole or main
residence, that the 100% premium for second homes would continue to
be applied in 2026/27.
 
This was seconded by Councillor
Carrington.
 
Councillor Harrington arrived at 5.20pm.
 
Members thanked officers for the significant
amount of work involved in preparing the budget despite pressures
from central government regarding funding. The pressures around
borrowing were noted and that capital expenditure was not without
risk. Notable pressures such as local government reorganisation and
support for rural businesses were also highlighted.
 
Following the late confirmation of the Local
Government Finance Settlement, the finance team had worked swiftly
to adjust proposals. While there were global uncertainties,
significant projects were still progressing. The 2.9% Council Tax
increase was supported and deemed necessary to maintain essential
services and the importance of NKDC continuing as responsible
guardians of the district during an uncertain period of
reorganisation was stressed.
 
It was noted that borrowing money within local
government should not be compared to personal borrowing, as it
supported the capital programme which had structured payback
arrangements. The long term investment opportunities within the
rolling 10 year programme were emphasised.
 
There were concerns that government appeared
intent on scrutinising reserves, however it was stressed that any
authority not preparing adequately for reorganisation would face
